Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Power Generation Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Power Generation's Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Jonathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Carter, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Reyes, Chief Operating Officer, and Lisa Chen, Chief Strategy Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jonathan Hale.

Jonathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1.  Strong earnings per share performance and key drivers.
    2.  Disciplined capital expenditure plan and project progress.
    3.  Outperformance in authorized versus earned return on equity.
    4.  Robust forward-looking guidance and strategic implications.
    5.  Management's views on prevailing industry trends and hurdles.

Let me provide some more detail on these five key aspects.

Starting with earnings per share, which really stood out this quarter and highlights the resilience of our diversified portfolio and our focused execution in the midst of the shifting energy transition. On an adjusted basis, we achieved EPS of $1.52, beating the consensus view of $1.48 and showing a strong 12% rise from $1.36 in the second quarter of last year. This is our sixth straight quarter of double-digit EPS growth, validating the success of our Reliable Renewables approach.

For context, GAAP EPS was $1.41, with the $0.11 gap mostly from a one-time mark-to-market gain on our nuclear decommissioning trust, offset by restructuring costs tied to optimizing our older coal plants. Stripping those out, adjusted EPS shows genuine operational leverage. Let me unpack the main contributors: revenue growth first, then cost controls, and balance sheet factors.

Revenues hit $2.3 billion adjusted, up 8% from last year, thanks to better power prices and higher volumes from our merchant assets, which make up 45% of our 28 GW capacity. In PJM, our main Northeast hub, energy prices averaged $68 per MWh, 22% higher than prior year, driven by a severe June heat wave that pushed system lambdas over $200 per MWh on peak days. Our 4.5 GW gas-fired combined-cycle plants, averaging a 7,200 Btu/kWh heat rate, grabbed significant margins, adding $0.18 to EPS via smart dispatch and our proprietary Steam Cycle Ramp Management tech, hitting 98.5% equivalent availability.

Performance varied by region but netted out positively. In ERCOT, boosted by our 2023 Lone Star Renewables buy, LMPs averaged $52 per MWh, held back by wind surplus but lifted by data center demand now at 15% of Texas peaks. Our 1.2 GW BESS there played volatility for $0.09 EPS gain with 85% round-trip efficiency and ancillary services. In MISO South, softer weather and solar curtailments kept prices at $45 per MWh, but our 2024 BRA capacity wins for 2.3 GW at $250 per kW-year gave a steady $0.06 EPS boost, locking 85% of 2025-2026 capacity cash flows.

On the regulated front, Apex Utilities in the Northeast posted 4% load growth from electrification, with EVs at 12% penetration, yielding $0.45 EPS from ROE-allowed returns on a $1.2 billion rate base build. Our renewables shift amplified this: 450 MW of community solar and wind came online in Q2, tapping 30% ITC transferability via IRA Section 6418 for $180 million in credits and $0.12 EPS lift. Renewables are now 38% of our mix, up from 25% in 2022, with 42% blended capacity factor, balancing merchant potential with lower carbon exposure.

Shifting to expenses and fuel, adjusted EBITDA reached $850 million, up 14%, adding $0.24 to EPS from opex savings and hedging. Plant O&M fell 7% to $220 million via our AI predictive maintenance across 80% of the fleet, cutting forced outages 25% with digital twin tech for turbines—similar to NextEra's tools but customized for our gas-renewable hybrid. Fuel shone too: nat gas at $3.25 per MMBtu realized (90% hedged at $2.90 floor), down 15% YoY despite Henry Hub swings from LNG ramps. Coal-to-gas switches at three sites improved heat rates 8%, and CCUS pilots on peakers prep for 45Q credits in 2025. These countered a $0.03 EPS hit from labor and T&D inflation, holding utility O&M at 18% of revenues.

Balance sheet moves capped it off. D&A up 10% to $320 million from $2.5 billion 2023 capex mainly BESS and solar, but FFO to debt improved 200 bps to 18% after $500 million ATM equity at 12x forward P/E. Interest rose $15 million from variable loans for 1 GW Texas BESS, but all-in debt cost is 4.2% after our oversubscribed May green bond. Tax rate at 22%, down from 25%, via IRA elective pay on clean hydrogen from nuclear uprates (300 MW electrolyzer at Salem), adding $0.07 EPS—like Dominion's H2 moves.

Challenges included a $0.05 EPS drag from MISO coal penalties, eased by retirements, and Connecticut rate case lags deferring $100 million T&D. Weather-adjusted, EPS was $1.48, still above guide.

Forward, this sets FY2024 adjusted EPS at $5.85 to $6.05, 10-13% growth, Q3 $1.65-$1.75. Catalysts: 700 MW renewables, PJM reruns, 500 MW hyperscaler PPA at $55 per MWh. Risks like ERCOT outages or rates covered by 2.5x interest coverage, $1.8 billion liquidity.

In short, $1.52 EPS shows our integrated model—regulated base, merchant edge, renewables scale—driving steady growth like Duke and Vistra.

Next, our capital expenditure plan and project advances, central to delivering reliable, affordable clean power to 15 million customers in Southeast, Midwest, Northeast areas.

2024 total CAPEX guided at $7.8 billion, up 12% from $7.0 billion in 2023, speeding clean transition, grid hardening, transmission mandates, offset by cost discipline despite supply issues. Five-year to 2028: $42 billion, 9% CAGR, 45% renewables, 35% T&D, rest gen maintenance, nuclear extensions, long-duration storage.

Generation CAPEX $3.2 billion, 41%. Renewables 65%: on pace for 2.5 GW solar PV, 1.2 GW onshore wind by year-end, hitting 18 GW total renewables early vs 2025 goal.

Standouts: Magnolia Solar Plus Storage in Georgia, 750 MW solar + 300 MWh Fluence Cube, 85% built, first power this quarter, $850 million total with $120 million IRA ITCs, Q4 COD under Georgia Power PPA at <$35/MWh LCOE.

Midwest Prairie Wind Farm Phase II in Illinois, 400 MW added last month ahead via Vestas V236-15.0 MW turbines, 80% hedged at $45/MWh to 2030 against MISO negatives.

Thermal: $900 million gas/nuclear. Riverton CCGT South Carolina, 1,000 MW GE Vernova H-class, 60% done, H2 2025 COD for data center peaks, >64% efficiency. Nuclear $450 million uprates/replacements at three units, 15% uprate Salem Harbor Unit 2 for 1,200 MW extra by 2026, NRC-okayed to 2050+.

T&D $2.9 billion, 37%, up 18% on FERC 1920, post-Idalia hardening. Southeast SERC: $1.1 billion 500 kV reconductoring ACCC, 1,200 circuit-miles double capacity. Piedmont-to-Coastal 345 kV, $650 million 150-mile line energized, LOLE from 1-in-10 to 1-in-50.

Northeast PJM $800 million smart grid: synchrophasors, Siemens ADMS, 5,000 DERs via OpenADR, 200 MW DR last quarter. Midwest MISO: $400 million Badger-to-Clover HVDC vs wind curtailments.

BESS $650 million, 8%: 1.1 GWh YTD, Ironwood 200 MW/800 MWh ERCOT merchant, >15% IRR, arbitrage $150/MWh. Pipeline 3.5 GWh by 2026, Tesla Megapacks.

Focused on decarbonization (85% gen CAPEX Scope 1/2 cuts), electrification (4-5% load growth to 2030), resilience. IRA $2.5 billion credits lift after-tax ROE to 10.5%.

Risks: steel +8%, transformers +25%, but 70% 2025 locked. Reg lag PJM 18 months, 95% approvals. 20% T&D undergrounding cuts SAIDI 25% Florida.

Overall, CAPEX targets 8-10% reg ROE, 6-8% EPS growth, ESG lead. $42 billion plan flexible for storage/offshore if H2 offtake.

Third, our authorized versus earned ROE, key for regulated ops, showing execution vs benchmarks. Authorized ROE is regulator-set (FERC wholesale transmission, state PUCs Northeast/Midwest/Texas retail), basis for rates covering equity return, O&M, dep, taxes.

Earned ROE is actual from ops, capex, throughput. Premium proves outperformance via costs, utilization, investments.

TTM to June 30, 2024: earned 10.45% vs authorized blended 9.75%, 70 bps premium—eighth straight quarter above, up from 20 bps Q2 2023. Added $145 million equity earnings YoY, ~$0.12/share. Equity rate base up 8.2% to $18.7 billion, $2.1 billion net adds, $62 million AFUDC at earned rate.

Q2 2024: 10.62% earned vs 9.75% auth (87 bps); Q1 10.38% (63 bps); Q2 2023 9.95% (20 bps).

Drivers: ops leverage, cap efficiency, reg wins.

1. Ops: 4.1% retail load growth, 15% data center surge Texas AI boom. O&M flat 2.3% revs, down 150 bps via asset mgmt, predictive maint 25 GW fleet. CCNGs like 1,200 MW Riverton at 92% CF > auth, vs $2.85/MMBtu Henry Hub.

2. Capex: 650 MW solar+storage service ahead, Eldorado Valley 300 MW +200 MWh LFP batts, $28 million AFUDC, LCFS/PTC upside. CWIP Nevada earns on WIP.

3. Reg: Northeast case up 25 bps to 10.15% clean lead. FERC 10.25% Order 872, $41 million Q2 true-up.

By region: PJM Northeast auth 10.15% earned 10.88% +73 bps—capacity offsets, undergrounding full recovery. MISO Midwest 9.60% earned 10.12% +52 bps—HVDC Greenlink 85% util data centers. ERCOT Texas 9.50% earned 10.01% +51 bps—heat peaks 12 GW, Palo Verde-like nuclear 93% CF. FERC wholesale 10.25% earned 10.55% +30 bps—Path upgrades congestion relief. Blended 9.75%/10.45% +70 bps.

Risks: gas moderation, FERC cuts to 9.75-10%; stress 50 bps cut to 20 bps premium still good.

Outlook: 60-100 bps premium to 2026, $7.5 billion capex 40% renewables 2 GW, 30% trans offshore pilots, 30% modern AMI/DERMS. Q4 Texas case 9.85% ROE CWIP Gemini Solar Equinix/Google PPAs.

This ROE story confirms superior returns in decarbonizing grid.

Fourth, forward-looking outlook and implications. First safe harbor: today's talk incl guidance, projections, initiatives are forward-looking per 1995 Act, based on current expectations as of August 1, 2024, risks could vary materially: reg changes FERC/state RPS, commodity vol natgas/power, supply turbine/batt, weather, data center/EV demand shifts. No update duty but SEC 10-K/10-Q risks.

Entering 2025 strong from Q4 $485 million adj EBITDA +12% YoY, 92% nuclear CF, PJM $270/MW-day coal-gas converts.

2025 adj EBITDA $1.95-2.10 billion, 8-13% over 2024; Henry $3.20-3.50/MMBtu LNG, ERCOT $35-45/MWh data loads. EPS $4.85-5.25, 10% mid, O&M 18% revs, AFUDC $2.3 billion capex.

FCF pre-growth $1.1-1.3 billion funds $650 million divs 65-70% payout. BBB+ , $4 billion liq $2.5 billion revolver vs Dominion/Entergy rates.

Fleet shift: 28 GW to 45% renewables/storage by 2027 from 28%, IRA PTC/ITC, state clean goals Virginia 100% 2050.

Milestones: nuclear 4 GW Surry/North Anna 150 MW renewals to 2036, 94% CF, $120 million EBITDA EPU like Exelon.

Renewables 1.2 GW solar+storage 2025-26 PJM/MISO $45-55/MWh 85% hedged; Blue Ridge 400 MW First Solar CuTel 12%+ IRR. Wind 600 MW Oklahoma SPP GE 6MW 40-42% CF.

BESS 1.5 GWh by 2026, 500 MW/2 GWh ERCOT HB North, $200/MWh arb 4hr, 15% anc rev 25% CAGR like Vistra Moss.

Carbon to 350 lbs/MWh 2027 from 520, de-risk RGGI $18-22/ton.

Regions: PJM 8 GW BRA 2025-26 $300/MW-day gas 55% HR. ERCOT 3 GW 15% load to 450 GW peak, 20 GW data, 1 GW CCAs $60/MWh MSFT/Google.

Southeast reg ROE 10.25% $800 million rate base grid post-Helene, $450 million trans $100 million anc.

Mitigate curtailment 80/20 hybrid vPPAs tech.

Capex 2025 $2.2-2.5 billion 40% prod 35% ren/stor 25% T&D, 8-10% EPS ROIC 9-11%.

M&A: $1.2 billion 800 MW MISO coal repower gas-CCUS like NRG. Green H2 $2/kg 200 MW DOE.

AI Predix 2% O&M, NuScale SMR data baseload 95% up.

Sensitivities: $1 gas EBITDA $120 million; 5% data +$150 million. FERC 2023 +$500 million ROE. Risks ITC delay supply bifacial, 70% hedge.

7-9% EPS CAGR to 2028 > S&P Utils 300 bps, diversified incentives electrification.

Fifth, our take on industry trends and challenges. As top integrated utility/power gen with 25+ GW gas/renewables/nuclear, at pivotal shift: electrification/decarb/demand boom, headwinds reg/supply/capex.

Tailwinds: demand surge, EIA 2.6% CAGR to 2025 but we see 4.2% AI/data. Footprint PJM/MISO/ERCOT 5%+ YoY Q2, AWS/MSFT 10 GW+ PPAs. Data 45 GW by 2030 =40 Hoovers.

Renewables: solar LCOE -89% wind -70% Lazard. Our 2.5 GW solar+stor 32% CF Q2 bifacial First Solar 1.2 GWh Tesla. Global 510 GW 2023 IRENA China/India/EU REPowerEU.

Our $4.2 billion 2024 capex 60% ren: 1.8 GW CAISO/SPP queue, 500 MW H2-gas Texas. RECs +15% prem 12% EBITDA clean vs 8% thermal.

Regions: ERCOT 4 GW gas 85 GW peaks 65% CC CF $150/MWh. PJM 2700 GW queue delays 800 MW batt to 2027, IRA 45X/48E 30-40% IRR.

Europe TTF €35/MWh post-Ukraine, North Sea 500 MW Vestas JV 50% CF Siemens 15 MW. Asia China $0.22/W Philippines 300 MW $35/MWh PPA. Australia NEM 35% rooftop favors 200 MWh BESS.

Challenges:

1. Capex: $1.7T US to 2030 WoodMac ROE 10-8.5% rates. Our $12B 5yr 9.2% reg ROE, unfinanced overruns steel+12% turbine 36mo. Duke defer $6B; we 70/30 green bonds 4.8%.

2. Supply/interconnect: trans 95% ABB delay 20% solar, Nevada 400 MW slip Siemens. FERC 2023 cut queues 80% 2026, EEI hedge 50% EPC.

3. Reg/policy: IRA $370B but election PTC/ITC risk 25% clean returns. EU CBAM €10/ton LNG. State RPS CA 60%2030 +8% costs, TX 30% vol.

4. Weather/commodity/cyber: heat $5B outages NOAA. Henry $2.50 Q2 $3.80 winter, 60% hedge 10% exp. $150M NERC CIP post-Colonial.

5. Dispatch gap/tech: batt $140/kWh 4hr no gas replace. NuScale SMR $60/MWh 95% 2029 pilot. H2 $3/kg electro 60% eff Plug 50 MW.

Response: Power 2030 50% clean: 15 GW ren 5 GW stor 3 GW CCUS gas 1 GW SMRs.

Diversify 40% reg 35% contracted ren 95% PPAs Google/Meta 25% merchant.

R&D $500M long-dur Form iron-air AI dispatch -15% O&M.

JVs GE HA Brookfield $2B 12% yields.

ESG net-zero 2045 Scope2 -25% nuclear 93% CF.

Trends bullish demand/costs, $50B capex discipline. 6-8% EPS Q3 $1.45-1.55.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Emily Carter to discuss the financials.

Emily Carter: Thank you, Jonathan. Good morning, everyone. For the second quarter, we reported earnings per share of $1.52 and revenue of $2.3 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $1.95 billion, primarily focused on renewables and transmission upgrades. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate FY2024 adjusted EPS of $5.85 to $6.05.

Michael Reyes: Thank you, Emily. Let me provide an update on the operational front. We are seeing improved efficiency in our gas-fired combined-cycle power plants due to the implementation of our AI-powered predictive maintenance platform. This has resulted in a 15% increase in output while reducing forced outage rates by 25%.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Michael. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the long-duration energy storage space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth.

Jonathan Hale: Thank you, Emily, Michael, and Lisa. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for capital expenditure allocation in renewables?

Jonathan Hale: Certainly. Our CAPEX remains heavily weighted toward renewables, with 65% of generation spend going there this year. Projects like the Magnolia Solar Plus Storage at 750 MW paired with 300 MWh batteries are 85% complete, set for Q4 under a strong PPA. Similarly, Prairie Wind Phase II added 400 MW ahead of schedule. This builds our portfolio to 18 GW by year-end, capturing IRA benefits and hedging against volatility.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: What is your outlook for EPS growth into 2025?

Emily Carter: Our raised 2025 adjusted EPS guidance is $4.85 to $5.25, reflecting 10% midpoint growth. This assumes moderate nat gas pricing, data center load ramps in ERCOT and PJM capacity strength. FCF supports dividends while funding organic growth, with sensitivities well-hedged.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Kim: How are you mitigating risks related to supply chain bottlenecks?

Michael Reyes: We're addressing this head-on with 70% of 2025 commitments locked via long-lead contracts, despite steel and transformer inflation. For interconnection delays in PJM's queue, we're pushing FERC reforms and using fixed-price EPCs. Post-storm hardening and undergrounding have improved resilience, cutting outage impacts significantly.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Jonathan Hale for closing remarks.

Jonathan Hale: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the second quarter, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Apex Power Generation for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Apex Power Generation.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
